text_a: There are three types of interchange reimbursement fees (IRFs).

Domestic Interchange Reimbursement Fees—Fees paid by one participant to another for transactions acquired and issued in the same country. Intraregional Interchange Reimbursement Fees—Fees paid by one participant to another for transactions acquired and issued in different countries within the same Visa region. Interregional Interchange Reimbursement Fees—Fees paid by one participant to another for transactions acquired and issued in different Visa regions. In this context, transaction country is the country in which the transaction takes place, and issuing country is the country of the issuer of the card used in the transaction. If no domestic IRF has been established, the intraregional IRF applies. If no intraregional IRF has been established, the interregional (international) IRF applies. IRFs are settled daily through the settlement process. For National Net Settlement Service transactions, there is only one settlement currency, so balancing does not involve currency conversion. For International Settlement Service transactions, however, there are many settlement currencies. Visa uses buy and sell rates for currency conversion. These rates are paired into USD-based rates used when converting non- USD currencies against the U.S. dollar, and cross-rates (non-USD-based rates) used for selected currencies in which the rates quoted are against a currency other than the U.S. dollar. The Multicurrency Service automatically converts the transaction currency to the acquirer's settlement currency (if the two are different), and automatically converts the cardholder's billing currency to the issuer's settlement currency (if the two are different), to one of the settlement currencies. For POS transactions, IRFs are typically paid by acquirers to issuers. Fees for manual cash disbursements, reversals, merchandise returns, dispute financials, and credit adjustments flow in the opposite direction. The VisaNet Cashback Service identifies the cashback amount separately in authorization messages and in settlement to allow issuers to make authorization decisions and to monitor cash activity for their cardholders, Clients can contact their Visa representatives for additional information on cashback features, controls, and availability. Quasi-Cash – Quasi-cash is a variation of the purchase transaction, used for the purchase of items directly convertible to cash, such as gaming chips and money orders. It is available for Visa POS and Interlink. VisaNet does not support American Express Quasi-cash transactions. Key-Entered Purchase – This transaction is a variation of the purchase transaction, used only for Visa POS transactions when the magnetic stripe on the card is not readable. Purchase With Address Verification – This transaction is used by such merchants as direct marketing firms and airlines to verify a cardholder's address as part of a purchase request. This transaction is available for Visa POS.

Account Funding Transaction – This transaction is used to fund accounts such as brokerage accounts and online stored value cards, from a Visa debit or credit card. Original Credit Transaction – This transaction enables funds to be credited to Visa account numbers for a purpose other than refunding a Visa purchase. Deferred Clearing Purchase Transaction – This transaction is used by such merchants as hotels and car rental agencies when the full purchase amount is not known at the time of transaction authorization. This transaction, used only by Visa POS acquirers, involves an authorization request followed by a deferred clearing advice message. Merchandise Return – A merchandise return transaction enables merchants to credit the account of a Visa POS cardholder who returns merchandise. Balance Inquiry – Balance inquiry transactions enable cardholders to check their balances at stand-alone merchant terminals and at the point of sale. If the issuer system cannot be reached, V.I.P. stand-in processing responds that issuer is not available. If the issuer is available and supports balance inquiries, VisaNet returns the account balance to the acquirer for display or for printing in the currency of the merchant or of the ATM. Issuers can optionally provide balance information in Visa POS purchase transaction responses. However, for an 0200 POS eFunds transactions (network 0029), the acquirer receives balance information in Field 54 – Additional Amounts regardless of the issuer's selected response options. (This processing does not apply to stand-alone balance inquiries.) ATM acquirers in the U.S. region must support balance inquiries; support of this transaction is optional for all other participants. PINs are required for full service 0200 POS balance inquiries. PINs may not be required if a chip card is being used in a full service 0100 POS balance inquiries. Address Verification Only (Visa POS) – This transaction is used by merchants like direct marketing firms and airlines to verify a cardholder's address before submitting a purchase transaction. Incremental Authorizations – Merchants use incremental authorization transactions when final purchase amounts are unknown. Incremental authorizations enable merchants to obtain approval on additional amount, after the merchant uses an estimated amount to initiate and authorize the original transaction. Merchants can only do an incremental authorization in conjunction with an estimated authorization. When merchants determine final amounts, they submit supplemental, incremental authorization, or authorization reversal for cancelled purchases. Endpoints must not decline incremental authorizations by treating them as duplicate. In incremental authorization requests and their reversals, field 11 and field 37 values matches corresponding values in original authorization requests and the Transaction identifier (TID) value matches corresponding values in original authorization responses. Acquirers perform clearing using a single clearing transaction for the final amount, the issuer can match the incremental authorizations to the original estimated amount. Participating CPS POS Acquirers must include the TID from the initial authorization in any subsequent incremental authorization request or reversal.

paragraphs_matched.text_a: The Dynamic Key Exchange (DKE) Service is an optional service that enables clients to change Data Encryption Standard (DES) cryptographic keys with VisaNet through the use of online 0800 and 0810 messages. The following fields in the 0800 request are used for a DKE Service key exchange request: Field 11—System Trace Audit Number Field 33—Forwarding Institution Identification Code Field 39—Response Code Field 48, Usage 14—Dynamic Key Exchange Working Key Check Value Field 52—Personal Identification Number (PIN) Data Field 53—Security-Related Control Information Field 63.1—Network ID Code Field 70—Network Management Information Code Field 105—Double-Length DES Key (Triple DES) Field 110—Encryption Data (TLV Format) Clients use 0800 requests to request and to deliver new working keys for PIN encryption; clients use 0810 responses to acknowledge their receipt. paragraphs_matched.text_a: Other than the system-induced advice recovery, there are no system requirements that dictate when, or how often, clients should recover advices. An acquirer or an issuer can recover advices throughout the day or only during certain periods as it sees fit. When an issuer designs its system, however, it should consider the impact of STIP authorization on advice recovery processing. STIP advices reflect authorization decisions that can affect the available funds in a cardholder's account. If the issuer restricts advice recovery only to certain periods, it may find that account balances are insufficient to cover the total value of issuer- approved and STIP-approved transactions.
